summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -6 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Soybean meal +8.7%; weakest: Orange juice -14.1%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.85% (-15 bp in a month), 2-year 4.61% (-7 bp); 2s10s curve +24 bp (-8 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.16% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.92 (+1.7% in a month, +5.7% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.571 (+4.1% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.644 (-0.4%); USD/MXN 19.64 (+5.1%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -6.7% in a month (+5.6% YTD); VIX 27.0. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 83.96 $/bbl (-16.9% in a month), Brent 91.10, ULSD 3.723 $/gal (-18.6%), natural gas 3.52 (+1.3%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -17.5% in a month, Shanghai Composite -2.0%, Hang Seng -1.7%, yuan +0.4% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 10 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (30%); S&P GSCI -12.9% in a month; gold -10.1%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
